rows.abstract: Rationale: Among a host of development problems that includes poverty, social inequities and injustice, various population factors contributed and continue to contribute to stunting the full development of Filipinos. It has also severely reduced thecapability of government to provide basic services, further develop the rural areas and stem the tide of rapid urbanization and migration. > This bill, guided by the above principles and the multi-faceted nature of the problems besetting the countryand its people, proposes tht the State ultimately recognize the interdependence between population, development and environment.

rows.author: A105
rows.title_full: AN ACT CHANGING THE TITLE OF ALL LEGISLATIVE BODIES IN THE PROVINCIAL, CITY, MUNICIPAL AND BARANGAY LEVEL FROM SANGGUNIANG PANLALAWIGAN, SANGGUNIANG PANLUNGSOD, SANGGUNIANG PAMBAYAN AND SANGGUNIANG BARANGAY TO BATASAN PANLALAWIGAN, BATASAN PANLUNGSOD, BATASAN BAYAN AND BATASAN BARANGAY, RESPECTIVELY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 467, 468, 457, 458, 446, 447, 390, 391, 392, 393 OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The SANGGUNIAN, as a Filipino word is a misnomer in local governance as it means "consultant, counselor or adviser" and therefore illogical as the former never functions as a consultant but as a legislative body.  The term "Batasan" is the most appropriate title in order to impart the true meaning of the council as the body which enacts local laws and resolutions, and definitely, not merely a consultant or adviser to the chief executives.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE USE OF FUEL WOOD IN THE FLUE-CURING OF VIRGINIA TOBACCO AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: Admittedly, the Virginia tobacco industry has its share in the unabated denudation of our forests and destruction of our trees. This is because said industry depends on trees and forest resources for the fuel inputs of flue-curing barns for Virginia tobacco leaves. >On the other hand, the Virginia tobacco industry is so vital to be cursed and phased out as millions of people depend on it for livelihood and constitute a major source of  government revenues. > This bill therefore seeksto offer a compromise solution to the problem.

rows.abstract: For purposes of this Act, DIFFERENTLY-ABL ED INDIVIDUALS shall refer to a person with mental or physical disability, i.e. disability or incapacity caused by physical defect or infirmity, or bodily imperfection, which includes, but is not limited to,the blind, deaf, mute, amputees, paraplegics. The State shall also promote non-formal indigenous and out-of-school study programs, particularly those that respond to community needs, and to the needs of the marginalized sectors like the differently-abl ed women and children.

rows.abstract: "DEFAULT PROXY CEILINGS" refer to the required rates that would apply in case of failure to agree on charges between and among local telecommunicati on carriers within the period prescribed by the National Telecommunicati ons Commission. PROVIDED THAT DEFAULT PROXY CEILINGS SHALL BE AUTOMATICALLY EFECTIVE IN THE EVENT THAT THE LOCAL EXCHANGE CARRIERS OR TELEPHONE PROVIDERS ARE UNABLE TO AGREE ON EQUITABLE INTERCONNECTION CHARGES, WITHIN THE PERIOD SPECIIFIED BY THE COMMISSION. PROVIDED FURTHERTHAT THE EFFECTIVITY OF THE DPC SHALL IMMEDIATELY CEASE ONCE THE INTERCONNECTING CARRIERS HAVE REACHED AN AGREEMENT ON THE ACCESS CHARGE OR RATE.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GUARANTEE THE FREEDOM OF ACCESS TO INFORMATION FOR ALL JOURNALISTS, MEDIA PRACTITIONERS, AND CITIZENS OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Freedom of Information Act of 1999". This bill shall cover only agencies within the executive branch of government and constitutional bodies, EXCLUDING any office within the judicial and legilsative branches of government. Rationale: Gaining access to government-held information has been a problem for journalists and citizens alike. Journalists and the general public can do little when requests for information is denied.  Many government officials are reluctant in providing easy access bynews reporters and the general public to the vast amounts of information held by agencies within the government. and yet, access to these information is necessary for the efficient operation of our democracy.
